About this module Syllabus Units

Welcome to the Canvas module for the honours project in Computing, which is part of the programmes for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. Everything you need to know about doing the project will be found here.

The honours project is also referred to as a Capstone: An activity that rounds off your university experience, bringing together ideas from different topics, applying these ideas to new problems, and exploring them in depth. At the same time, the project prepares you for life after university through an emphasis on independent study and professional conduct.

The project is an independent piece of work worth 60 credits. That's half your credits in the final year, so you should expect to spend about half of your time this year working on your project.

60 credits roughly corresponds to 600 hours of work. That's a big number, how much is 600 hours? Well, there are about 7 months between the start of the project in the Autumn semester and the final submission deadline in Spring. That's roughly 210 days, so 600 hours are just under 3 hours every day from start to finish, including on weekends and holidays. Alternatively, if you could work full-time (40 hours/week) on the project, it would take about 15 weeks, or 3.5 months.

Although the project is your work, you have help: your supervisor guides you through the year, there will be various training sessions on the general skills you need, and there will be opportunities to get support and feedback from other staff. Most importantly, you have support from your peers: collectively, you are the most well-informed people about doing the honours project in 2026/27.

All information about learning materials, assessments and classes can be found in these Canvas pages; explore the materials using the Syllabus or Modules links. We don't want to overwhelm you, so information will be published step by step rather than all in one go.

To get you started, make sure you familiarise yourself with some key areas in this module. For example, Syllabus is where you can find key dates and a module outline. Modules is the place for information about this module and all your learning content.

Find support: Time at university can be exciting, but it can also feel stressful or overwhelming at times. If at any point during the year you feel like you’re struggling or need support, please remember you are not alone. We are here to help. Please reach out to your Module Leader (via the Key Contacts page) or your Project Adviser.

Alternatively, navigate to 'Key Support Routes' to find more sources of support available to you including the University's Student Learning Services and/or Mental Health and Wellbeing Service.
